requested_by: Tyler: 'Test 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 leg parlays as round robins with every combination of bets'

legs.edge: same as parlays_prereg.json P2: college shop-vs-sharp research bets at your books (spreads EV >= 4%, totals/moneylines EV >= 2%, -200..+200, one per game per market, first sight), 2021-2025; slate = kickoff week (Mon-Sun)
legs.ordinary: same as parlays_prereg.json P1: closing spreads at -110 with a random side (seed 7), college FBS vs FBS 2021-2025; each week N games drawn at random (seed 7)

formats: for each week, take N picks (edge: the N highest-EV legs from different games; N = 4..10, plus 'all' = every leg that week); bet EVERY combination of k legs from different games, k = 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 (k <= N), and 'k = 2-6' = every combination of every size together (one round robin with all of them). Equal stake per parlay, total weekly stake = 1 unit. Compared with the same N picks bet as singles (1 unit split evenly).
payout: as parlays_prereg.json: product of leg odds; pushed legs drop out; same-game legs never combined
metrics: per format and period: realized ROI, CLV-implied ROI (product of (1 + leg CLV) - 1, averaged), share of losing weeks, worst week, largest drawdown (weeks of stake)
pass: a format beats singles only if in BOTH development and holdout its realized ROI and CLV-implied ROI exceed singles' (same N) and its largest drawdown is <= 1.5x singles'. Many formats are tried (about 45), so a single pass is weak evidence; any pass becomes a candidate for its own pre-registered paper track, not a recommendation.
do_not_edit: do not change after seeing results
